mc.q: Ana has a job offer paying 3,000 per month. A second company offers her 2,800. Which concept explains why she can turn it down calmly?
mc.why: Her BATNA is the other offer of 3,000: if there is no deal, she still has it. A target point is what she hopes to get, not her plan B.

options: The worst deal you would still accept
The best deal you can imagine
mc.why: It is the worst deal you would still accept; below it you prefer your BATNA. The first offer is about anchoring, not your limit.

open.q: You are selling your bike and a friend already offered you 200. Explain your BATNA and reservation point, and how you would use them.
points: BATNA: selling to the friend for 200
Reservation point close to 200, derived from the BATNA
Do not reveal the reservation point
A strong BATNA lets you ask for more
open.model: My BATNA is selling the bike to my friend for 200, because that is what I can do if this negotiation fails. My reservation point is therefore about 200: I would not accept less from a new buyer. I would not reveal that number, because the buyer would then offer exactly 200. Since my alternative is solid, I can ask for more than 200 and walk away calmly if the buyer refuses.
